messages.subject: HMM AR1
parts:
Hi

I am trying to build a HMM AR(1) model with potentially more than 2 states. I am struggling with the `state` matrix. Every t-th row should be a simplex. I am obviously doing something wrong with the indexing of `state`.

It would also be nice to keep kk[T] as a parameter but int params are not allowed.

data {
  int T;
  int K;  // states
  real y[T];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=-1, upper=1> phi[K];
  real<lower=0> alpha[K];
  simplex[K] state[T, K];
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  real<lower=0> sigma_s;
}
model {
  int kk;
  alpha ~ normal(mean(y), 1);
  phi ~ normal(.5, .5);
  for (i in 1:K)
    state[1, i] ~ beta(1.0 / K, 1.0);
  for (t in 2:T) {
    for (i in 1:K) {
      state[t, i] ~ normal(state[t - 1, i], sigma_s);
    }
    kk ~ categorical(to_vector(state[t, ])); // compiler fails
    y[t] ~ normal(alpha[kk] + phi[kk] * y[t - 1], sigma);
  }
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] HMM AR1
parts:
Stan doesn't allow discrete parameters. When you write this

> model {

> int kk;
...
kk is not defined when you hit the sampling statement. Given

you'll see that state[t, ] (which is equal to state[t] and state[t, , ])
will be an array of vectors. There's no to_vector function that applies
to arrays of vectors, nor is that likely to be what you want to do here.

What you need to do is look in the manual for how to marginalize
the discrete parameters out of an HMM.

And the priors you have on the simplexes don't make sense (the initial simplex
gets independent betas, where you probably want a Dirichlet), and the subsequent
ones get normals, which is probably not what you want for simplex-constrained
parameters. Maybe something that works on the logit scale?

- Bob
